newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 24.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:

* NEW YORK - At least two major institutional shareholders in Walt Disney Co will vote against Disney Chairman and CEO Michael Eisner's contract at the company's annual meeting Tuesday. The College Retirement Equities Fund and the California Public Employees Retirement System are objecting to Eisner's new 10-year employment deal, which is worth at least $300 million. The two also plan to withhold their support for the five Disney directors standing for re-election -- including Disney vice chairman Roy Disney. Former Disney president Michael Ovitz's severance pay, worth at least $90 million, is not a subject for vote at the meeting.

* HOLLYWOOD - "The Empire Strikes Back" by News Corp's Twentieth Century Fox earned an estimated $22.3 million at its box office opening over the weekend. The movie's lifetime haul is now at $245 million, while "Star Wars," which topped the chart for the previous three weeks, moved into the No. 2 slot. Third and fourth place went to "Absolute Power" and "Dante's Peak," with projected weekend grosses of $9 million and $7 million, respectively.

* HOLLYWOOD - News Corp's Twentieth Century Fox Television has a multiyear development deal with Clive Barker's Seraphim Films to develop and produce primetime series, movies of the week and children's programming. The multimillion-dollar deal with Twentieth is part of an overall relationship the production company's parent News Corp. has with Barker.

* HOLLYWOOD - Director Tony Scott's next directing job and "Leaving Las Vegas" star Elisabeth Shue's next role are two of the major projects that Scott Free Productions has unveiled. Domino is the true story of Domino Harvey, a former Ford Agency model who became a female bounty hunter. Shue is attached to star in "Where the Money Is," a comedy.
* HOLLYWOOD - The cast of "The Birdcage" took a top Screen Actors Guild Award, as did Geoffrey Rush for "Shine" and Frances McDormand for "Fargo." In TV categories, "Seinfeld" by NBC won two awards.
